questions.title: Salary Net Percentage Change (Percentages)
questions.description: A company increases an employee's salary by 20% and then decreases it by 10%. What is the overall percentage change in the salary?

mcqData.explanation:
Assume original salary is 100.
After 20% increase: 100 × 1.20 = 120.
After 10% decrease: 120 × 0.90 = 108.
Overall increase = 108 - 100 = 8% increase.

questions.title: Combined Efficiency (Time & Work)
questions.description: A can complete a task in 12 days and B in 24 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish the task?

mcqData.explanation:
A's 1-day work = 1/12. B's 1-day work = 1/24.
Combined 1-day work = 1/12 + 1/24 = 3/24 = 1/8.
Therefore, working together they finish the task in 8 days.

questions.title: Round Trip Average Speed (Time, Speed & Distance)
questions.description: A driver travels from City A to City B at a speed of 40 km/h and returns along the same route at 60 km/h. What is the average speed for the entire journey?

mcqData.explanation: For equal distance, Average Speed = 2xy / (x + y) = (2 × 40 × 60) / (40 + 60) = 4800 / 100 = 48 km/h.

questions.title: HCF & LCM Product Relation (HCF & LCM)
questions.description: The HCF of two numbers is 11 and their LCM is 693. If one number is 77, find the other number.

mcqData.explanation:
Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM.
77 × X = 11 × 693 => X = (11 × 693) / 77 = 693 / 7 = 99.

questions.title: Word Letter Arrangements (Permutation & Combination)
questions.description: In how many different ways can the letters of the word "LEADER" be arranged?

mcqData.explanation:
The word "LEADER" has 6 letters in total with "E" repeating twice.
Total arrangements = 6! / 2! = 720 / 2 = 360.

questions.title: Rolling Two Dice Probability (Probability)
questions.description: Two unbiased six-sided dice are rolled simultaneously. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers is 8?

mcqData.explanation:
Favorable outcomes for sum = 8: (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2) = 5 outcomes.
Total outcomes = 36.
Probability = 5/36.

questions.title: 1. Tell Me About Yourself
questions.description: Tell me about yourself.

hrData.sampleAnswer: I am a Computer Engineering student with a strong interest in software development and problem-solving. During my academic journey, I have worked on projects involving web development, databases, APIs, and programming. I have also completed an internship where I gained practical exposure to working on real-world tasks and understanding professional development practices. Along with technical skills, I have been actively improving my problem-solving, communication, and teamwork abilities. Currently, I am focused on strengthening my coding, DSA, database, and core computer science skills so that I can contribute effectively in a professional role.
hrData.whyThisWorks:
- Covers education and technical background.
- Mentions practical experience.
- Shows continuous learning.
- Ends with a career-focused statement.
hrData.improveItBy: Add one specific project achievement and one measurable result.

questions.title: 2. What Are Your Strengths?
questions.description: What are your strengths?

hrData.sampleAnswer: My main strengths are that I am a quick learner, persistent, and comfortable solving problems step by step. When I encounter something I do not know, I first try to understand the problem, research possible approaches, and then practice until I can implement it confidently. I also take responsibility for my work and try to communicate clearly with my teammates.
hrData.whyThisWorks:
- Gives relevant strengths.
- Explains them instead of simply listing them.
- Connects strengths to workplace behavior.
hrData.improveItBy: Mention a real example demonstrating one of these strengths.

questions.title: 3. What Is Your Weakness?
questions.description: What is your biggest weakness?

hrData.sampleAnswer: Earlier, I sometimes spent too much time trying to make a solution perfect before moving forward. I realized that this can affect productivity, so I have been working on prioritizing tasks, setting time limits, and first completing a reliable solution before improving it. This has helped me become more practical and efficient.
hrData.whyThisWorks:
- Gives a genuine but manageable weakness.
- Does not present a critical professional flaw.
- Shows self-awareness and improvement.
hrData.avoid:
- "I have no weaknesses."
- "I am a perfectionist" without explaining how you manage it.
- Mentioning weaknesses that directly prevent you from performing the job.

questions.title: 4. Why Should We Hire You?
questions.description: Why should we hire you?

hrData.sampleAnswer: You should hire me because I have a strong willingness to learn, a solid foundation in programming and computer science concepts, and practical project experience. I am comfortable learning new technologies and working through problems systematically. I may still be at the beginning of my professional career, but I am willing to put in the effort required to learn quickly, take responsibility, and contribute to the team.
hrData.whyThisWorks:
- Confident without sounding arrogant.
- Focuses on value.
- Appropriate for a fresher or early-career candidate.
hrData.improveItBy: Connect your skills directly to the job description.

questions.title: 5. Why This Company?
questions.description: Why do you want to join our company?

hrData.sampleAnswer: I am interested in joining your company because the role provides an opportunity to apply my technical knowledge to real-world problems while continuing to learn from experienced professionals. I am particularly interested in the kind of projects and technologies involved in this role. I believe the environment would allow me to grow professionally while contributing through my problem-solving skills, willingness to learn, and technical foundation.
hrData.improveItBy:
Research the company before the interview and mention:
- A product
- A technology
- A recent initiative
- The company's engineering culture
- Something specific about the role

A company-specific answer is much stronger than a generic one.

questions.title: 6. What Are Your Short-Term Goals?
questions.description: What are your short-term career goals?

hrData.sampleAnswer: My short-term goal is to start my career in a role where I can apply my programming and problem-solving skills to real-world projects. I want to strengthen my technical skills, understand professional development practices, and become a dependable team member. I also want to continuously improve through feedback and hands-on experience.

questions.title: 7. What Are Your Long-Term Goals?
questions.description: What are your long-term career goals?

hrData.sampleAnswer: My long-term goal is to become a strong and dependable technology professional who can take ownership of complex problems and contribute to important projects. As I gain experience, I would like to develop deeper technical expertise, take greater responsibility, and eventually mentor other team members.
hrData.avoid: Giving a long-term plan that suggests you will quickly leave the company.

questions.title: 8. What Is Your Biggest Achievement?
questions.description: What is your biggest achievement?

hrData.sampleAnswer: One of my biggest achievements has been successfully completing a project from planning through implementation while learning technologies that were new to me. The experience required me to understand requirements, solve technical issues, debug problems, and complete the work within the available time. More than the final result, I consider the ability to learn independently and complete the project a significant achievement.
hrData.improveItBy:
Use the **STAR method**:

- Situation
- Task
- Action
- Result

Add a measurable result whenever possible.

questions.title: 9. What Is Your Biggest Failure?
questions.description: Tell me about a failure or mistake.

hrData.sampleAnswer: One mistake I made during a project was underestimating the amount of time required for some technical tasks. As a result, some work had to be completed under tighter time constraints than expected. I learned the importance of breaking large tasks into smaller parts, estimating time more realistically, and keeping some buffer for unexpected problems. Since then, I have become more careful about planning and tracking my work.
hrData.whyThisWorks:
- Accepts responsibility.
- Does not blame others.
- Shows learning and improvement.

questions.title: 10. Tell Me About Your Teamwork Experience
questions.description: Tell me about a time you worked in a team.

hrData.sampleAnswer: During an academic project, I worked with teammates where we divided the project into different responsibilities. We regularly discussed progress, helped each other with technical issues, and integrated our individual work into the final project. I learned that effective teamwork is not only about completing your own task but also about communicating clearly and helping the team achieve the overall objective.
hrData.improveItBy:
Mention:
- Team size
- Your responsibility
- A problem
- How you solved it
- Final result

questions.title: 11. Tell Me About Your Leadership Experience
questions.description: Tell me about a time you demonstrated leadership.

hrData.sampleAnswer: During a group project or team activity, I took responsibility for coordinating tasks, discussing deadlines, and making sure everyone understood their responsibilities. When problems came up, I tried to bring the team together to discuss possible solutions rather than making decisions alone. This experience taught me that leadership is mainly about taking responsibility, communicating clearly, and helping others succeed.
hrData.improveItBy: Use a real leadership example and quantify the result.

questions.title: 12. How Do You Handle Conflicts?
questions.description: How do you handle conflicts with teammates?

hrData.sampleAnswer: I try to handle conflicts calmly and focus on the problem rather than the person. First, I listen to the other person's perspective and try to understand the reason for the disagreement. Then I explain my perspective and look for a solution based on the project's requirements and facts. If necessary, I involve a senior or team lead to reach a fair decision.

questions.title: 13. How Do You Handle Stress?
questions.description: How do you handle stress or pressure?

hrData.sampleAnswer: When I am under pressure, I first prioritize the tasks based on urgency and importance. I break large tasks into smaller steps and focus on completing them one at a time. I also communicate early if I identify a potential issue instead of waiting until the deadline. This helps me remain organized and maintain the quality of my work.

questions.title: 14. Are You Willing to Relocate?

I would be happy to discuss the compensation based on the overall role and benefits.

questions.title: 16. How Would You Explain a Gap?

hrData.sampleAnswer: During that period, I focused on improving my skills and preparing myself for the next opportunity. I used the time to work on programming, projects, interview preparation, and technical concepts relevant to my career. Although the period was not part of formal employment or education, it helped me become more prepared and focused professionally.

questions.title: 17. Tell Me About Your Internship

hrData.sampleAnswer: During my internship, I gained practical exposure to working on technical tasks in a professional environment. I worked with relevant technologies, understood project requirements, solved implementation and debugging issues, and learned how development work is organized. The internship helped me understand the difference between academic projects and real-world development, especially in terms of requirements, deadlines, collaboration, and testing.

Through this project, I improved my programming, database, debugging, and problem-solving skills.
